description: Redevelopment of site by erection of 2-storey dwelling house with habitable loft space, one front and two rear dormers, side roof lights, raised rear patio, new vehicular access, hardstanding, boundary treatments and associated landscaping and refuse and cycle storage.

decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

No development above ground level shall commence until details of the external finishing materials including brickwork; brick detailing such as soldier course & render banding, plinth and entrance door detail; roof materials and junctions inc. parapets, dormer, roof edge, ridge and eaves; window and door openings and installations including frame, panels and window bars have been submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.A schedule of materials and their use in the approved scheme is required and samples made available on site. A photograph showing all samples to be inspected must be submitted. The development shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure a satisfactory external appearance.

The development shall not commence until a Construction Traffic Management Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The statement should include:a)	photographic condition survey of public carriageways, verges and footways in the vicinity of the site; b)	map showing routeing of demolition and construction vehicles to/from the site;The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved construction management plan unless otherwise agreed by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure construction does not lead to damage of the nearby public road network and to minimise disruption to the neighbouring properties.

Prior to the commencement of the development hereby approved (including demolition and all preparatory work), a scheme for the protection of all retained trees compliant with BS 5837:2012 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The scheme will comprise a detailed Arboricultural Method Statement (AMS) report supplemented by Tree Protection Plans (TPP) for both demolition and construction stages. The plans shall be of legible scale and clearly show the layout (as agreed), all relevant existing site features that form a consideration within the protection scheme, and the location/extent of all appropriate protection measures.Specific matters to be addressed within the AMS and TPPs will include:a)	methods of demolition of existing structures and boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to Root Protection Areas (RPA - as defined within BS 5837:2012); b)	removal of existing hard standing and kerb edging within or directly adjacent to RPAs;c)	details of all construction that necessitate level changes within RPAs;d)	details and specification of foundations within RPAs and their installation methodology;e)	details and specification of all utility services/drainage/SUDs features within RPAs (where unavoidable) and their installation methodology;f)	a full specification for the construction of all, paths, parking areas and driveways (including alterations to the existing layout of internal hard standing) within RPAs. Where a no-dig sub-base is specified (e.g. cellular confinement system) a specification shall be provided (including a diagrammatical cross-section of the product in-situ) and extent of areas where this would be implemented illustrated within the TPP;g)	detailed levels and cross-sections to show that the raised levels of surfacing where the installation of no-dig surfacing within RPAs is proposed, demonstrating that the raised areas can be effectively integrated with prevailing levels where they meet with adjacent surfacing or building damp proof courses;h)	a full specification for the installation of boundary treatments within or directly adjacent to RPAs;i)	a specification for protective fencing and, if necessary, ground protection, to safeguard all trees during both demolition and construction phases. The Tree Protection Plan(s) shall clearly indicate the alignment of the fencing and extent of ground protection;j)	a specification for scaffolding and ground protection in Construction Exclusion Zones (where necessary); k)	details of site access, temporary parking, on site welfare facilities, loading, unloading and storage of equipment, materials, fuels and waste as well concrete mixing and siting of fires;The development thereafter shall be implemented in strict accordance with the approved details.Reason: Required prior to commencement of development to satisfy the Local Planning Authority that the trees to be retained will not be damaged during demolition or construction and to protect and enhance the appearance and character of the site and locality, in accordance with Policy DMD80 (Trees on Development Sites) and pursuant to section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

Prior to completion or first occupation of the development hereby approved, whichever is the sooner; full details of 10 trees to be planted and establishment shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Priority should be given to planting larger trees and indigenous species, or other species of high ecological value  , where situations allow. The details shall include;o	Tree species, nursery sizes in accordance with BS:3936-1 :1992, and quantities.o	Locations on a plan marked with existing trees and their canopy spreads/RPAs, with all other relevant landscape/built features.o	Details of supplier, delivery, timescales and handling on site.o	Detailed step by step planting methodology in accordance with BS8545:2014Support systems:o	Cross section drawings showing planting pit, tree, support systems etc.Aftercare plans:All tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with those details and at those times. Any trees that are found to be dead, dying, severely damaged or diseased within five years of the completion of the building works OR five years of the carrying out of the landscaping scheme (whichever is later), shall be replaced in the next planting season by specimens of similar size and species in the first suitable planting season.Reason: To comply with the duties indicated in Section 197 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 to safeguard and enhance the amenity of the area, to maximise the quality and usability of open spaces within the development, and to enhance its setting within the immediate locality in accordance with NPPF 136, Policies G7 (A) of the London Plan (2021), DMD 81 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014) and HW-7 of the Hadley Wood Neighbourhood Plan (2023).

Prior to the commencement of development, a Dust Management Plan (DMP), based on an Air Quality and Dust Risk Assessment (AQDRA), shall be submitted to and approved, in writing, by the local planning authority. The DMP shall be in accordance with The Control of Dust and Emissions during Construction and Demolition SPG 2014. The DMP will need to detail the measures to reduce the impacts during the construction phase. The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved plan.During each four construction sub-phases of the proposed development (demolition, earthworks, construction, and trackout), PM10 continuous monitoring shall be carried out on site. Parameters to be monitored, duration, locations and monitoring techniques must be approved in writing by the London Borough of Enfield prior to commencement of monitoring.Reason: To protect the local amenity from demolition/construction dust.

Prior to the commencement of the development, evidence of site registration at http://nrmm.london/ to allow continuing details of Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) and plant of net power between 37kW and 560 Kw to be uploaded during the construction phase of the development shall be submitted to and approved by the Local Planning Authority.Evidence that all plant and machinery to be used during the demolition and construction phases of the development shall meets Stage IV of EU Directive 97/68/ EC for both NOx and PM emissions shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority.During the course of the demolitions, site preparation and construction phases, an inventory and emissions records for all Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) shall be kept on site. The inventory shall demonstrate that all NRMM is regularly serviced and detail proof of emission limits for all equipment. All documentation shall be made available for inspection by Local Authority officers at all times until the completion of the development.Reasons: In the interests of good air quality and protecting public health.

Prior to occupation of the development, details of the means of enclosure shall submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The enclosure around the vehicular access shall not exceed 0.60m in height where it encroaches within 2.0m of either side of the vehicle access point. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved detail unless otherwise agreed with the Local Planning Authority. Reason: Safety of vulnerable road users is paramount, therefore, to ensure viability of pedestrians the footway (including children and buggies who are shorter and cannot be easily seen), vehciles must be able to see the whole footway clearly when exiting the premises as well as the carriageway prior to moving.

The development shall not be occupied until the existing vehicular access has been reinstated at the expense of the applicant. This condition should be read in conjunction with the Informative also attached to the permission. REASON: In the interests of street scene and on street parking provision.

Notwithstanding drawing ref: 37LA-302 Revision C, the development shall not be occupied until details of the proposed new vehicle access has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.. The approved crossover should be installed in full prior to the occupation of the development and be retained perpetually. This condition should be read in conjunction with the Informative also attached to the permission. REASON: In the interests of street scene and on street parking provision.

Prior to occupation, the renewable energy technologies included in the  approved Energy Statement shall be incorporated into the development and installed in accordance with the recommendations of the Energy Statement.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

All areas of hedges, scrub or similar vegetation where birds may nest which are to be removed as part of the development, are to be cleared outside the bird-nesting season (March - August inclusive) or if clearance during the bird-nesting season cannot reasonably be avoided, a suitably qualified ecologist will check the areas to be removed immediately prior to clearance and advise whether nesting birds are present. If active nests are recorded, no vegetation clearance or other works that may disturb active nests shall proceed until all young have fledged the nest.Reason: To ensure that wildlife is not adversely impacted by the proposed development in accordance with national wildlife legislation and in line with CP36 of the Core Strategy. Nesting birds are protected under the Wildlife and Countryside Act, 1981 (as amended).

Prior to occupation details of bird boxes shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The details shall include the exact location, specification and design of the habitats.The nesting boxes shall be provided strictly in accordance with the details so approved, installed prior to the first occupation of the building to which they form part or the first use of the space in which they are contained and shall be maintained as such thereafter.Reason: To provide positive gains for biodiversity.

Prior to occupation, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Surface Water Drainage Strategy Report dated August 2025 and (drawing: SuDS hardstanding) before it is occupied. REASON: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF.

Prior to occupation details of refuse storage facilities including facilities for the recycling of waste to be provided within the development, in accordance with Enfield Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Development 2024 shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter maintained unless otherwise in writing by the Local Planning Authority.In particular, waste collection vehicles must be able to get within 25m of the refuse storage point. Residents should not have to carry waste further than 30m.Reason: In order to facilitate efficient, safe and clean removal of household refuse, the location and accessibility of refuse storage plus to maintain safety on the Highway.

Prior to occupation, the development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved cycle parking details as set out in (drawing ref: 37LA-302 Revision C and Highway Impact Assessment). The cycle parking shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), the Council's adopted standards and London Cycling Design Standards Chapter 8.

Notwithstanding the details set out in Part G Water Efficiency Report (21.07.2025), the development must achieve reduced water consumption through the use of water efficient fittings, appliances and recycling systems to result in consumption equal to or less than 105 litres per person per day.Reason: To promote water conservation and efficiency measures in all new developments and where possible in the retrofitting of existing stock in accordance with Core Policy 21 of the Core Strategy and the London Plan.

Prior to occupation of the development, the windows to be installed on the ground and first floor side elevation facing No.39 Lancaster Avenue shall be in obscure glass and fixed shut to a height of 1.7 metres above the floor level of the room to which they relate.The glazing shall not be altered without the approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To safeguard the privacy of the occupiers of neighbouring properties.

Notwithstanding the provisions of Classes A, B and, F , Schedule 2, Part 1 and Class A of Schedule 2, Part 2 of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015, or any statutory instrument revoking and re-enacting this Order, no buildings, extensions or alterations to buildings or development the curtilage of buildings (of a nature related to the aforementioned Classes within the Order), shall be undertaken without the formal written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To maintain a satisfactory appearance, neighbouring residential amenities and adequate private amenity space for future occupiers.
